annotation.paper_title: DLP Dynamic Layerwise Pruning in Large Language Models
annotation.caption: WikiText validation perplexity of LLaMA1-7B, LLaMA1-13B and Vicuna-7B pruned by various M at 70% sparsity using OWL.
annotation.annotation: The line plot illustrates the WikiText validation perplexity of three different models, LLAMA1-7B, LLAMA1-13B, and Vicuna-7B, as a function of the parameter M. The x-axis represents the variable M, with a linear scale ranging from 3 to 8, and tick labels at integer intervals. The y-axis denotes perplexity, also on a linear scale, ranging from 20.0 to 40.0, with tick labels at intervals of 10. The blue line, representing Vicuna-7B, uses triangular markers with a solid line. It begins at a perplexity of about 41.0 at M=3, trends sharply downward to about perplexity of about 35.0 when M=4, decreases slightly till it reach a minimum perplexity of about 33.0 at M=7, and increases to around 39.0 at M=8. The green line, representing LLAMA1-7B, uses circular markers and a solid line style. It begins at a perplexity of about 28.0 at M=3, reaches a minimum of around 25.0 at M=5, and increases to around 36.0 at M=8. The orange line, representing LLAMA1-13B uses star markers with a solid line. It begins at a perplexity of 20.0 at M=3, decreases to about perplexity of about 15.0 at M=6, and then increases to around 20.0 at M=8. A legend positioned near the center-right of the plot defines each line by its corresponding model name, marker shape and color. Each line has a different pattern and they do not intersect.
annotation.model_annotation: The plot illustrates the perplexity of three different models, LLAMA1-7B, LLAMA1-13B, and Vicuna-7B, as a function of the parameter M. The x-axis represents the variable M, with a linear scale ranging from 3 to 8, and tick labels at integer intervals. The y-axis denotes perplexity, also on a linear scale, ranging from 20.0 to 40.0, with tick labels at intervals of 5. The green line, representing LLAMA1-7B, utilizes circular markers and a solid line style. It begins at approximately 35.0 perplexity at M=3, reaches a minimum of around 29.0 at M=5, and increases to about 36.0 at M=8. The orange line for LLAMA1-13B features star-shaped markers with a solid line. It starts at approximately 23.0 at M=3, decreases to a low point of near 21.0 at M=6, and then returns to around 23.0 at M=8. The blue line, indicative of Vicuna-7B, uses triangular markers with a solid line. It begins at a perplexity of about 38.0 at M=3, trends downward to reach a minimum of approximately 32.0 at M=5, and rises back to around 38.0 at M=8. Each line demonstrates a distinct pattern across the range of M values.

annotation.paper_title: DLP Dynamic Layerwise Pruning in Large Language Models
annotation.caption: WikiText validation perplexity of LLaMA1-7B, LLaMA1-13B and Vicuna-7B pruned by various M at 70% sparsity using OWL.
annotation.annotation: The line plot illustrate the perplexity of three different models, LLAMA1-7B, LLAMA1-13B, and Vicuna-7B, against a parameter M on validation set of WikiText dataset. The x-axis represents parameter M, with a linear scale with values ranging from 3 to 8 at an interval of 1. The y-axis denotes perplexity, also on a linear scale, ranging from 20.0 to 40.0, with tick labels at intervals of 10. The green line, representing LLAMA1-7B, utilizes circular markers and a solid line style. It begins at M=3, with a perplexity of approximately 28.0 and then at M=5, it has minimum perplexity of 25.0, and then it increases to about 35.0 at M=8. The orange line for LLAMA1-13B features star-shaped markers with a solid line. It starts at approximately 20.0 at M=3, reaches its minimum at M=6, and then returns to around 19.0 at M=8. The blue line with triangular markers, indicative of Vicuna-7B. It begins at a perplexity of about 41.0 at M=3, trends downward to reach a minimum of approximately 34.0 at M=7, and rises back to around 39.0 at M=8. A legend is also provided at the centre right of plot which map the different colors of line to their LLM architecture names.
annotation.model_annotation: The plot illustrates the perplexity of three different models, LLAMA1-7B, LLAMA1-13B, and Vicuna-7B, as a function of the parameter M. The y-axis denotes perplexity, also on a linear scale, ranging from 20.0 to 40.0, with tick labels at intervals of 5. The green line, representing LLAMA1-7B, utilizes circular markers and a solid line style. It begins at approximately 35.0 perplexity at M=3, reaches a minimum of around 29.0 at M=5, and increases to about 36.0 at M=8. The orange line for LLAMA1-13B features star-shaped markers with a solid line. It starts at approximately 23.0 at M=3, decreases to a low point of near 21.0 at M=6, and then returns to around 23.0 at M=8. The blue line, indicative of Vicuna-7B, uses triangular markers with a solid line. It begins at a perplexity of about 38.0 at M=3, trends downward to reach a minimum of approximately 32.0 at M=5, and rises back to around 38.0 at M=8. Each line demonstrates a distinct pattern across the range of M values.

annotation.paper_title: DLP Dynamic Layerwise Pruning in Large Language Models
annotation.caption: WikiText validation perplexity of LLaMA1-7B, LLaMA1-13B and Vicuna-7B pruned by various M at 70% sparsity using OWL.
annotation.annotation: The line plot illustrates the WikiText validation perplexity of three different models, LLAMA1-7B, LLAMA1-13B, and Vicuna-7B, as a function of the parameter M. The x-axis represents the variable M, with a linear scale ranging from 3 to 8, and tick labels at integer intervals. The y-axis denotes perplexity, also on a linear scale, ranging from 20.0 to 40.0, with tick labels at the intervals of 10. The orange line denoting LLAMA1-13B features star-shaped markers with a solid line. Initially it starts at approximately 23.0 at M=3, gradually decreases to a low point of near 21.0 at M=6, and then increases back to approximately 23.0 at M=8. The green line, representing LLAMA1-7B, uses circular markers and a solid line style. It starts at approximately 28.0 perplexity at M=3, reaches a minimum of around 25.0 at M=5, and increases back to around 36.0 at M=8. The blue line, representing Vicuna-7B, makes use of triangular markers with a solid line. It begins at a perplexity of around 41.0 at M=3, gradually moves downward to reach a minimum of approximately 32.0 at M=6, and rises back to around 39.0 at M=8. Each line demonstrates a distinct pattern, and there is no intersection among them across the range of M values.

annotation.paper_title: DLP Dynamic Layerwise Pruning in Large Language Models
annotation.caption: WikiText validation perplexity of LLaMA1-7B, LLaMA1-13B and Vicuna-7B pruned by various M at 70% sparsity using OWL.
annotation.annotation: The line plot shows the perplexity of different LLM models with respect to a varying parameter M. The x-axis represents the variable M with a linear scale ranging from 3 to 8, with tick labels at an integer interval of one. The y-axis represents perplexity on a linear scale, ranging from 20.0 to 40.0, with tick labels at intervals of 5. The green line representing LLAMA1-7B, uses circular markers and a solid line style. It begins at approximately 28 perplexity at M=3, reaching a minimum of around 25 at M=5, and increases to about 36.0 at M=8. The orange line for LLAMA1-13B features star-shaped markers with a solid line. It starts at approximately 20 at M=3, decreases to a low point of near 16.0 at M=6, and then returns to around 20 at M=8. The blue line, indicative of Vicuna-7B, uses triangular markers with a solid line. It begins at a perplexity of about 41 at M=3, trends downward to reach a minimum of approximately 35 at M=6, and rises back to around 38 at M=8. Each line demonstrates a distinct pattern across the range of M values.

It begins at approximately 35.0 perplexity at M=3, reaches a minimum of around 29.0 at M=5, and increases to about 36.0 at M=8. The orange line for LLAMA1-13B features star-shaped markers with a solid line. It starts at approximately 23.0 at M=3, decreases to a low point of near 21.0 at M=6, and then returns to around 23.0 at M=8. The blue line, indicative of Vicuna-7B, uses triangular markers with a solid line. It begins at a perplexity of about 38.0 at M=3, trends downward to reach a minimum of approximately 32.0 at M=5, and rises back to around 38.0 at M=8. Each line demonstrates a distinct pattern across the range of M values.

annotation.paper_title: DLP Dynamic Layerwise Pruning in Large Language Models
annotation.caption: WikiText validation perplexity of LLaMA1-7B, LLaMA1-13B and Vicuna-7B pruned by various M at 70% sparsity using OWL.
annotation.annotation: The line graph illustrates the WikiText validation perplexity of three models: LLaMA1-7B, LLaMA1-13B, and Vicuna-7B with varying M values. LLaMA1-7B is represented by a green line with circles, LLaMA1-13B is represented by a orange line with stars and Vicuna-7B is represented by a blue line with triangles. The x-axis represents the variable M ranging from 3 to 8, and the y-axis represents the perplexities ranging from 20.0 to 40.0. When M = 3, the perplexity of LLaMA1-7B (green line) starts from perplexity = 35.0, decreases to its lowest perplexity = 29.0 when M = 5, finally increases to 36.0 when M = 8. The perplexity of LLaMA1-13B (orange line) starts from perplexity = 23.0 when M = 3, decreases to lowest perplexity = 21.0 when M = 6, reaches its peak perplexity = 23.0 when M = 8. The perplexity of Vicuna-7B (blue line) starts from its highest perplexity at 38.0 when M = 3, decreases to its lowest point at perplexity = 32.0 when M = 5, and rises back to perplexity = 38.0 when M = 8. When M = 8, the perplexity for all three models increases.
annotation.model_annotation: The plot illustrates the perplexity of three different models, LLAMA1-7B, LLAMA1-13B, and Vicuna-7B, as a function of the parameter M. The x-axis represents the variable M, with a linear scale ranging from 3 to 8, and tick labels at integer intervals. The y-axis denotes perplexity, also on a linear scale, ranging from 20.0 to 40.0, with tick labels at intervals of 5. The green line, representing LLAMA1-7B, utilizes circular markers and a solid line style. It begins at approximately 35.0 perplexity at M=3, reaches a minimum of around 29.0 at M=5, and increases to about 36.0 at M=8. The orange line for LLAMA1-13B features star-shaped markers with a solid line. It starts at approximately 23.0 at M=3, decreases to a low point of near 21.0 at M=6, and then returns to around 23.0 at M=8. The blue line, indicative of Vicuna-7B, uses triangular markers with a solid line. It begins at a perplexity of about 38.0 at M=3, trends downward to reach a minimum of approximately 32.0 at M=5, and rises back to around 38.0 at M=8. Each line demonstrates a distinct pattern across the range of M values.

annotation.paper_title: DLP Dynamic Layerwise Pruning in Large Language Models
annotation.caption: WikiText validation perplexity of LLaMA1-7B, LLaMA1-13B and Vicuna-7B pruned by various M at 70% sparsity using OWL.
annotation.annotation: The plot illustrates the perplexity of three different models, LLAMA1-7B, LLAMA1-13B, and Vicuna-7B, as a function of the parameter M. The x-axis represents the variable M, with a linear scale ranging from 3 to 8. The y-axis represents perplexity, also on a linear scale, ranging from 15.0 to 40.0, with tick labels at intervals of 10. The green line, representing LLAMA1-7B, utilizes circular markers and a solid line style. It begins at approximately 28.0 perplexity at M=3, reaches a minimum of around 25.0 at M=5, and increases to about 36.0 at M=8. The orange line for LLAMA1-13B features star-shaped markers with a solid line. It starts with perplexity at 20.0 when M=3, decreases to about 16.5 when M=4, remains fairly stable up until when M=6, and then perplexity rises to about 21.0 when M=8. The blue line represents Vicuna-7B, and uses triangular markers with a solid line. It begins at a perplexity of about 40.5 when M=3, decreases sharply to about 35.0 when M=4, remains fairly stable until M=7, then rises to about 39.0 when M=8.

annotation.paper_title: DLP Dynamic Layerwise Pruning in Large Language Models
annotation.caption: Comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates. Due to the significant difference in values between high and low sparsity rates, we use the logarithmic results for comparison.
annotation.annotation: The bar chart illustrates the comparison of perplexity values of "Per-Output" and "Per-Layer" at different sparsity rates.The horizontal axis labeled "Sparsity rates", ordered sequentially from 10% to 80%, in increments of 10%. The vertical axis labeled "Perplexity", with a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^1 to 10^3, marked with regularly spaced tick labels at intervals corresponding to powers of 10. The chart features pair of bars for each sparsity rate with blue bar followed by orange bar, with blue bars representing Per-Output and orange bars representing Per-Layer. The approximate perplexity values of the bars increase with higher sparsity rates, starting from around 2 at 10% sparsity, and approaching 10^3 as sparsity reaches 80%. The values remains below 10^2 till 70% sparsity. At 70% and 80% sparsity, the bars exhibit a notable increase in height compared to the lower sparsity rates. At 60% the orange bar is slightly above 10^1 while the blue bar is still below 10^1. At 50%, 60%, 70% and 80% the orange bars are taller than the blue bars. The bars are not sorted in any particular order beyond the increasing sparsity rate. A legend positioned in the top-left corner of the figure defines each bar with "Per-Output" or "Per-Layer" and it's color.
annotation.model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the relationship between sparsity rate and perplexity, depicted through two different configurations: Per-Output and Per-Layer. The horizontal axis contains the categories labeled as sparsity rates, ordered sequentially from 10% to 80% in increments of 10%, with the axis labeled as "Sparsity Rate." The vertical axis represents the perplexity, labeled "Perplexity," with a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^1 to 10^3, marked with regularly spaced tick labels at intervals corresponding to powers of 10. The chart features grouped bars for each category, with blue bars representing the Per-Output configuration and orange bars representing the Per-Layer configuration. The approximate values of the bars increase with higher sparsity rates, starting from around 10 at 10% sparsity to over 100 and approaching 1000 as sparsity reaches 80%. At 70% and 80% sparsity, the bars exhibit a notable increase in height compared to the lower sparsity rates. The bars are not sorted in any particular order beyond the increasing sparsity rate, and none of the bars are visually emphasized with special shading, bolding, or outlining.

annotation.paper_title: DLP Dynamic Layerwise Pruning in Large Language Models
annotation.caption: Perplexity of LLaMA1-7B on different validation datasets under varying quantization bits.
annotation.annotation: The series of bar charts illustrates the perplexity values associated with different quantization bits for three datasets: WikiText, PTB, and C4. Each chart has the horizontal axis labeled as "Quantization Bits," displaying the categories in increasing order as 3, 4, 8, and 16. The vertical axis for each chart is labeled "Perplexity," with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 400 on the second chart and up to 30 on the first and third charts, with numerical tick intervals of 50 in the second chart and 5 in the first and third charts respectively. In each chart, the bars are grouped in pairs for each quantization bit category; the first bar of each pair is labeled "Uniform" and is colored blue, while the second bar is labeled "Ours" and is colored orange. In the WikiText chart, the height of the "Uniform" bars approximately ranges from 26 to 31, whereas the "Ours" bars range from 17 to 22. In the PTB chart, "Uniform" bars span approximately from 300 to 420, while "Ours" bars range from around 160 to 240. In the C4 chart, "Uniform" bars are approximately between 24 and 30, and "Ours" bars range from 17 to 20. The bars within each chart are consistently arranged by category for comparison without any specific sorting. A legend is present in top-left each chart, clarifying the colors associated with "Uniform" and "Ours". There is no particular emphasis or annotation on any individual bar in the charts.

annotation.paper_title: DLP Dynamic Layerwise Pruning in Large Language Models
annotation.caption: Perplexity of LLaMA1-7B on different validation datasets under varying quantization bits.
annotation.annotation: The series of bar charts illustrates the perplexity values associated with different quantization bits for three different datasets: WikiText, PTB, and C4. Each chart has the horizontal axis labeled as "Quantization Bits," represented in the categories in increasing order as 3, 4, 8, and 16. The vertical axis for each chart is labeled "Perplexity," with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 30 in first and third plot (WikiText and C4 dataset) and 0 to 400 in PTB dataset chart. In each chart, the bars are grouped in pairs for each quantization bit category; the first bar of each pair is labeled "Uniform" and is colored blue, while the second bar is labeled "Ours" and is colored orange. These represented the two sparsity levels: Uniform and papers (DLP pruned sparsity) respectively. In the WikiText chart, the height of the "Uniform" bars approximately ranges from 25 to 31 , whereas the "Ours" bars range from 16 to 21. In the PTB chart, "Uniform" bars span approximately from 300 to 400, while "Ours" bars range from around 100 to 240 approximately. In the C4 chart, "Uniform" bars are approximately between 24 and 30, and "Ours" bars range from 16 to 20. The bars within each chart are consistently arranged by category for comparison without any specific sorting. However, in each of the dataset, perplexity is decreasing as quantization bits increasing. A legend is present in top left of each chart, clarifying the colors associated with "Uniform" and "Ours."

The vertical axis for each chart is labeled "Perplexity," with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 400 on the second chart and up to 30 on the first and third charts, with numerical tick intervals of 50 and 5 respectively. In each chart, the bars are grouped in pairs for each quantization bit category; the first bar of each pair is labeled "Uniform" and is colored blue, while the second bar is labeled "Ours" and is colored orange. In the WikiText chart, the height of the "Uniform" bars approximately ranges from 25 to 30, whereas the "Ours" bars range from 15 to 20. In the PTB chart, "Uniform" bars span approximately from 300 to 400, while "Ours" bars range from around 100 to 200. In the C4 chart, "Uniform" bars are approximately between 20 and 30, and "Ours" bars range from 10 to 20. The bars within each chart are consistently arranged by category for comparison without any specific sorting. A legend is present in each chart, clarifying the colors associated with "Uniform" and "Ours." There is no particular emphasis or annotation on any individual bar in the charts.

annotation.paper_title: DLP Dynamic Layerwise Pruning in Large Language Models
annotation.caption: Perplexity of LLaMA1-7B on different validation datasets under varying quantization bits.
annotation.annotation: The series of bar charts illustrates the perplexity values associated with different quantization bits for three datasets: WikiText, PTB, and C4. Each chart has the horizontal axis labeled as "Quantization Bits," displaying the categories in increasing order as 3, 4, 8, and 16. The vertical axis for each chart is labeled "Perplexity," with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 400 on the second chart and up to 30 on the first and third charts, with numerical tick intervals of 50 and 5 respectively. In each chart, the bars are grouped in pairs for each quantization bit category; the first bar of each pair is labeled "Uniform" and is colored blue, while the second bar is labeled "Ours" and is colored orange. In the WikiText chart, the height of the "Uniform" bars approximately ranges from 25 to 30, whereas the "Ours" bars range from 18 to 22. In the PTB chart, "Uniform" bars span approximately from 300 to 450, while "Ours" bars range from around 170 to 250. In the C4 chart, "Uniform" bars are approximately between 25 and 30, and "Ours" bars range from 18 to 21. In all three charts and for each quantization bit category, the blue bar for "Uniform" is always higher than the orange bar for "Ours." annotation.annotation: The pie chart illustrates three different characters. The inner circle of the pie chart is divided into three segments of different characters : Virtual Characters represented in blue, Custom Characters represented in red, and Real Characters in green. These three segments are further divided into outer slices, shaded in lighter color. Virtual character segment is further subdivided into “Comic characters”, “Movie Characters”, “Teleplay Characters”, ”Novel Characters” and ”Game Characters”. Custom characters has one unlabeled slice. The real characters segment contains seven slices: ”Scientists”, ”Artists”, ”Athletes”, ”Writers”, ”Musicians”, Actors” and ”Influencers”.

annotation.annotation: The plot illustrates the absolute mean values of hidden states across different layers, providing a comparison before and after a gate, as well as against a baseline. The y-axis is labeled "Abs Mean" and has a linear scale ranging from 0 to 5 with tick labels at intervals of 1. There are three lines depicted in the plot. The blue dashed line, which represents the "hidden state mean before gate," starts with abosulte mean value close to 0 at layer 0 and exhibits a generally steady trend until around layer 17, where it climbs significantly, peaking at about 4.3 by layer 23. Both the solid green line and the dotted orange line, representing "hidden state mean of baseline" and "hidden state mean after gate" respectively, remain relatively constant at 0 accross all layers.

annotation.annotation: The line plot illustrates the absolute mean values of hidden states across different layers, providing a comparison before and after a gate, as well as against a baseline. The x-axis is labeled "Layer" with a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 20, and tick labels are marked at intervals of 5. The y-axis is labeled "Abs Mean" with a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 4, with tick labels at intervals of 1. There are three lines depicted in the plot. The first is a blue dashed line representing the "hidden state mean before gate, avg 0.71", which starts with Abs Mean approximately 0.01 in layer 0 and exhibits a generally steady increasing trend until around layer 17, where it climbs significantly, peaking at about 4.7 in layer 24. The second line is an orange dotted line representing the "hidden state mean after gate, avg 0.05", which starts with Abs Mean 0 at layer 0 and remains fairly constant across the layers, ending slightly below 0.1 in layer 24. The third line is a solid green line for the "hidden state mean of baseline, avg 0.04" beginning with Abs Mean around 0 at layer 0 and maintaining a nearly flat trajectory throughout, concluding near 0.04 in layer 24. The blue dashed line doesn't intersect with the other two lines, whereas the orange dotted line and green line intersect multiple times. A legend is located top left of the plot describing lines and their representation.

annotation.caption: Proportion of SDPA output values below threshold after gating (Left: 1e-2, Right: 1e-3). We also include sparsity measurements obtained by multiplying the average gating score with pre-gating hidden states.
annotation.annotation: The plot illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA output across different layers, using a threshold of 1e-2. The x-axis is labeled "Layer," and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 22 with tick labels at intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled "Sparsity Ratio," also employs a linear scale and spans from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. Three lines are present in the plot. The blue dashed, which represents the "sparsity ratio before gate", begins at about 0.2 ratio at layer 0, reduces to almost 0.0 by layer 2 and stays relatively constant accross all layers. The orange dotted line, representing "sparsity ratio after gate," starts at about 1.0 ratio at later 0, reduces to about 0.2 by layer 14, and shows flactuations between 0.2 and 0.4 thereafter. The green dash-dot line, representing the "sparsity ratio after average gate," starts at roughly 1.0, decreasing more smoothly to about 0.17 ration by layer 14 and then remains relatively stable with slight fluctuations thereafter.
annotation.model_annotation: The plot illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA output across different layers, under a threshold of 1e-2. The first line, represented by a blue dashed line with circle markers, shows the "sparsity ratio before gate" and begins at around 1.0, decreasing steadily to approximately 0.0 towards the right of the plot. The orange dotted line with no markers represents the "sparsity ratio after gate," starting at about 1.0 and reducing to near 0.1 by layer 10, with slight increases and fluctuations thereafter. The third line, a green dash-dot line with no markers, depicts the "sparsity ratio after average gate," beginning at roughly 1.0, decreasing more smoothly, and stabilizing near 0.1 by layer 15 with minor fluctuations in subsequent layers.

annotation.paper_title: Gated Attention for Large Language Models Non-linearity, Sparsity, and   Attention-Sink-Free
annotation.caption: Proportion of SDPA output values below threshold after gating (Left: 1e-2, Right: 1e-3). We also include sparsity measurements obtained by multiplying the average gating score with pre-gating hidden states.
annotation.annotation: The plot illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA output across different layers, under a threshold of 1e-2. The x-axis is labeled "Layer," using a linear scale ranging from 0 to 25, with tick labels at intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled "Sparsity Ratio," also uses a linear scale and ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, featuring tick labels at intervals of 0.2. There are three lines in the plot. The first line, represented by a blue dashed line, depicts the "sparsity ratio before gate" and begins at around 0.2, decreasing steadily to approximately 0.01 towards the right of the plot. The orange dotted line with circle markers represents the "sparsity ratio after gate," starting at about 1.0 and reducing to near 0.3 by layer 10, with slight increases and fluctuations thereafter. The third line, a green dash-dot line with dashed and circular markers, shows the "sparsity ratio after average gate," beginning at roughly 1.0, decreasing more smoothly, and stabilizing near 0.1 by layer 15 with minor fluctuations in subsequent layers. A legend is provided in the bottom right corner of the plot which identifies three lines and also provides their average sparsity ratio.

annotation.paper_title: Gated Attention for Large Language Models Non-linearity, Sparsity, and   Attention-Sink-Free
annotation.caption: Proportion of SDPA output values below threshold after gating (Left: 1e-2, Right: 1e-3). We also include sparsity measurements obtained by multiplying the average gating score with pre-gating hidden states.
annotation.annotation: The line plot illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA output across different layers, under a threshold of 1e-2. The x-axis is labeled "Layer", using a linear scale ranging from 0 to 20, with tick labels at intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled "Sparsity Ratio", also employs a linear scale and spans from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. Three lines are present in the plot. The first line, represented by a blue dashed line shows the "sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.03" and begins at Sparsity ratio around 0.2 at Layer 0, decreasing sharply to approximately 0.03 at Layer 3, and maintaining steady decrease towards the right of the plot till Layer 24. The orange dotted line represents the "sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.44" starting at Sparsity Ratio about 1.0 and reducing sharply to near 0.2 by layer 14, with slight fluctuations thereafter til 19 and higher fluctuations thereafter ending around Sparsity 0.4 at Layer 24. The third line, a green dash-dot line with no markers, depicts the "sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.33" beginning at Sparsity Ratio of about 1.0, reducing sharply to near 0.2 by layer 14, with slight fluctuations thereafter ending around Sparsity 0.05 at Layer 24. The blue dashed line doesn't intersect with the other two lines, whereas the orange dotted line and green dash-dot line intersect multiple times at the beginning. A legend is located top right of the plot describing lines and their representation.
annotation.model_annotation: The plot illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA output across different layers, under a threshold of 1e-2. The x-axis is labeled "Layer," using a linear scale ranging from 0 to 22, with tick labels at intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled "Sparsity Ratio," also employs a linear scale and spans from 0.0 to 1.0, featuring tick labels at intervals of 0.2. Three lines are present in the plot. The first line, represented by a blue dashed line with circle markers, shows the "sparsity ratio before gate" and begins at around 1.0, decreasing steadily to approximately 0.0 towards the right of the plot. The orange dotted line with no markers represents the "sparsity ratio after gate," starting at about 1.0 and reducing to near 0.1 by layer 10, with slight increases and fluctuations thereafter. The third line, a green dash-dot line with no markers, depicts the "sparsity ratio after average gate," beginning at roughly 1.0, decreasing more smoothly, and stabilizing near 0.1 by layer 15 with minor fluctuations in subsequent layers.

annotation.paper_title: Gated Attention for Large Language Models Non-linearity, Sparsity, and   Attention-Sink-Free
annotation.caption: Proportion of SDPA output values below threshold after gating (Left: 1e-2, Right: 1e-3). We also include sparsity measurements obtained by multiplying the average gating score with pre-gating hidden states.
annotation.annotation: The line plot illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA output across different layers, under a threshold of 1e-2. The x-axis is labeled "Layer," using a linear scale ranging from 0 to 20, with tick labels at intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled "Sparsity Ratio," also employs a linear scale and spans from 0.0 to 1.0, featuring tick labels at intervals of 0.2. Three lines are present in the plot. The first line, represented by a blue dashed line, shows the "sparsity ratio before gate" and begins at approximately 0.2 sparsity ratio, decreases abruptly at the layer 2 and decreasing steadily to approximately 0.0 towards the right of the plot. The orange dotted line with no markers represents the "sparsity ratio after gate," starting at about 1.0 and reducing to near 0.1 by layer 13, with slight increases and fluctuations thereafter and gradually decreases to around 0.05 at the layer 24. The third line, a green dash-dot line, depicts the "sparsity ratio after average gate," beginning at roughly 1.0, decreasing more smoothly and abruptly with less fluctuation till the layer approximately 13, and stabilizing near 0.1 by layer 15 with minor fluctuations in subsequent layers and slight increase in sparsity ratio back to around 0.4 at the layer 24.A legend is located top right of the plot, describing lines and their representation of different sparsity ratio.

annotation.paper_title: Gated Attention for Large Language Models Non-linearity, Sparsity, and   Attention-Sink-Free
annotation.caption: Proportion of SDPA output values below threshold after gating (Left: 1e-2, Right: 1e-3). We also include sparsity measurements obtained by multiplying the average gating score with pre-gating hidden states.
annotation.annotation: The line plot shows the sparsity ratio of SDPA output across different layers under a threshold of 1e-2. The x-axis is labeled "Layer", using a linear scale ranging from 0 to 20, with tick labels at intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled "Sparsity Ratio", also employs a linear scale and spans from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. The blue dashed line shows the "sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.03" and begins at Sparsity ratio around 0.2 at Layer 0, decreasing sharply to slightly above zero at Layer 3, and maintaining steady decrease towards the right of the plot till Layer 24. The orange dotted line represents the "sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.44" starting at Sparsity Ratio about 1.0 and reducing sharply to near 0.2 by layer 15, and increases with fluctuations ending around Sparsity 0.4 at Layer 24. The green dash-dot line depicts the "sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.33" beginning at a Sparsity Ratio of about 1.0, reducing sharply to near 0.2 by layer 15, with slight fluctuations thereafter ending slightly above 0 at Layer 24. The orange and green lines follow the same sharp declining trend. A legend is located top right of the plot describing lines and their representation.
annotation.model_annotation: The plot illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA output across different layers, under a threshold of 1e-2. The x-axis is labeled "Layer," using a linear scale ranging from 0 to 22, with tick labels at intervals of 5. The orange dotted line with no markers represents the "sparsity ratio after gate," starting at about 1.0 and reducing to near 0.1 by layer 10, with slight increases and fluctuations thereafter. The third line, a green dash-dot line with no markers, depicts the "sparsity ratio after average gate," beginning at roughly 1.0, decreasing more smoothly, and stabilizing near 0.1 by layer 15 with minor fluctuations in subsequent layers.

annotation.paper_title: Self-Interpretability LLMs Can Describe Complex Internal Processes that   Drive Their Decisions, and Improve with Training
annotation.caption: Results of Experiments 1 and 2. GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini can accurately report quantitative factors driving their decision-making across a great variety of scenarios, and fine-tuning on accurate explanation further improves their ability to do so. Left: Models were making choices based on preferences instilled in them by fine-tuning. Each point corresponds to a single attribute (e.g., condo ceiling height; 5 per choice contexts, 100 choice contexts). Location in the x-dimension corresponds to the weight that a model assigned to an attribute (as reflected in their decisions). Location in the y-dimension corresponds to the weight that a model reported assigning to that attribute when prompted explicitly. The weights the models reported meaningfully correlated with the weights that actually guided their decisions, and fine-tuning on examples of accurate reports further improved their accuracy. Right: The Pearson correlation between the models' reported and learned attribute weights before and after training (blue and purple, respectively). The reports of the base models that had not undergone this fine-tuning were almost entirely uncorrelated with the learned preferences (gray). Thus, the accuracy of the fine-tuned models must reflect their ability to report their new (fine-tuned) preferences and not an informed guess about their preferences based on their general background knowledge. Error bars indicate 95% HDIs.
annotation.annotation: The bar chart illustrates the self-report accuracy related to instilled preferences for two models, GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini, under different training conditions. The categories are displayed along the horizontal axis and include GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini, arranged in this order. The value axis is vertical, labeled as "Self-Report Accuracy (Instilled Preferences)" and ranges from 0.00 to 1.00 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 0.25. Each model category is represented by three bars: gray for "Control", light blue for "Before Introspection Training", and dark blue for "After Introspection Training", as indicated in the legend. For GPT-4o, the gray bar is the shortest, at approximately 0.10, the light blue bar is around 0.55, and the dark blue bar is nearly 0.75. For GPT-4o-mini, the gray bar is slighlty below 0.0, the light blue bar is approximately 0.50, and the dark blue bar is around 0.75. A legend is given Top left decsribing the category and their color.

annotation.paper_title: Self-Interpretability LLMs Can Describe Complex Internal Processes that   Drive Their Decisions, and Improve with Training
annotation.caption: Results of Experiments 1 and 2. GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini can accurately report quantitative factors driving their decision-making across a great variety of scenarios, and fine-tuning on accurate explanation further improves their ability to do so. Left: Models were making choices based on preferences instilled in them by fine-tuning. Each point corresponds to a single attribute (e.g., condo ceiling height; 5 per choice contexts, 100 choice contexts). Location in the x-dimension corresponds to the weight that a model assigned to an attribute (as reflected in their decisions). Location in the y-dimension corresponds to the weight that a model reported assigning to that attribute when prompted explicitly. The weights the models reported meaningfully correlated with the weights that actually guided their decisions, and fine-tuning on examples of accurate reports further improved their accuracy. Right: The Pearson correlation between the models' reported and learned attribute weights before and after training (blue and purple, respectively). The reports of the base models that had not undergone this fine-tuning were almost entirely uncorrelated with the learned preferences (gray). Thus, the accuracy of the fine-tuned models must reflect their ability to report their new (fine-tuned) preferences and not an informed guess about their preferences based on their general background knowledge. Error bars indicate 95% HDIs.
annotation.annotation: The bar chart illustrates the self-report accuracy related to instilled preferences for two models, GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini, under different training conditions. The categories are displayed along the horizontal axis and include GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini, arranged in this order. The value axis is vertical, labeled as "Self-Report Accuracy (Instilled Preferences)" and ranges from 0.00 to 1.00 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 0.25. Each model category is represented by three bars: gray for "Control," light blue for "Before Introspection Training," and dark blue for "After Introspection Training," as indicated in the legend. For GPT-4o, the gray bar is the shortest, at approximately 0.10, the light blue bar is around 0.55, and the dark blue bar is nearly 0.75. For GPT-4o-mini, the gray bar is about 0.0, the light blue bar is approximately 0.50, and the dark blue bar is around 0.75. Bars are grouped side by side within each model category and arranged such that the grey bar is the leftmost, followed by light blue, followed by dark blue. A legend is provided on the top left of the bar plot to map colors to their labels.

annotation.paper_title: Self-Interpretability LLMs Can Describe Complex Internal Processes that   Drive Their Decisions, and Improve with Training
annotation.caption: Results of Experiments 1 and 2. GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini can accurately report quantitative factors driving their decision-making across a great variety of scenarios, and fine-tuning on accurate explanation further improves their ability to do so. Left: Models were making choices based on preferences instilled in them by fine-tuning. Each point corresponds to a single attribute (e.g., condo ceiling height; 5 per choice contexts, 100 choice contexts). Location in the x-dimension corresponds to the weight that a model assigned to an attribute (as reflected in their decisions). Location in the y-dimension corresponds to the weight that a model reported assigning to that attribute when prompted explicitly. The weights the models reported meaningfully correlated with the weights that actually guided their decisions, and fine-tuning on examples of accurate reports further improved their accuracy. Right: The Pearson correlation between the models' reported and learned attribute weights before and after training (blue and purple, respectively). The reports of the base models that had not undergone this fine-tuning were almost entirely uncorrelated with the learned preferences (gray). Thus, the accuracy of the fine-tuned models must reflect their ability to report their new (fine-tuned) preferences and not an informed guess about their preferences based on their general background knowledge. Error bars indicate 95% HDIs.
annotation.annotation: The bar chart illustrates the self-report accuracy related to instilled preferences for two models, GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini, under different training conditions. The categories are displayed along the X-axis and include GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini, arranged in this order. The value axis is vertical, labeled as "Self-Report Accuracy (Instilled Preferences)" and ranges from 0.00 to 1.00 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 0.25. Each model category is represented by three bars: gray for "Control," light blue for "Before Introspection Training," and dark blue for "After Introspection Training," as indicated in the legend situated at the left top corner. For GPT-4o, the gray bar is the shortest, at approximately 0.10, the light blue bar is around 0.55, and the dark blue bar is nearly 0.75. For GPT-4o-mini, the gray bar is about 0.10, the light blue bar is approximately 0.50, and the dark blue bar is around slightly higher than 0.75.In both the models "After Introspection Training" condition has the highest accuracy with "Control" condition has the lowest .Bars are grouped side by side within each model category, without any specific sorting, and no bars are visually emphasized.

annotation.paper_title: Self-Interpretability LLMs Can Describe Complex Internal Processes that   Drive Their Decisions, and Improve with Training
annotation.caption: Results of Experiments 1 and 2. GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini can accurately report quantitative factors driving their decision-making across a great variety of scenarios, and fine-tuning on accurate explanation further improves their ability to do so. Left: Models were making choices based on preferences instilled in them by fine-tuning. Each point corresponds to a single attribute (e.g., condo ceiling height; 5 per choice contexts, 100 choice contexts). Location in the x-dimension corresponds to the weight that a model assigned to an attribute (as reflected in their decisions). Location in the y-dimension corresponds to the weight that a model reported assigning to that attribute when prompted explicitly. The weights the models reported meaningfully correlated with the weights that actually guided their decisions, and fine-tuning on examples of accurate reports further improved their accuracy. Right: The Pearson correlation between the models' reported and learned attribute weights before and after training (blue and purple, respectively). The reports of the base models that had not undergone this fine-tuning were almost entirely uncorrelated with the learned preferences (gray). Thus, the accuracy of the fine-tuned models must reflect their ability to report their new (fine-tuned) preferences and not an informed guess about their preferences based on their general background knowledge. Error bars indicate 95% HDIs.

Each model category is represented by three bars: gray for "Control", light blue for "Before Introspection Training", and dark blue for "After Introspection Training" as indicated in the legend. annotation.paper_title: Self-Interpretability LLMs Can Describe Complex Internal Processes that   Drive Their Decisions, and Improve with Training
annotation.caption: Results of Experiments 1 and 2. GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini can accurately report quantitative factors driving their decision-making across a great variety of scenarios, and fine-tuning on accurate explanation further improves their ability to do so. Left: Models were making choices based on preferences instilled in them by fine-tuning. Each point corresponds to a single attribute (e.g., condo ceiling height; 5 per choice contexts, 100 choice contexts). Location in the x-dimension corresponds to the weight that a model assigned to an attribute (as reflected in their decisions). Location in the y-dimension corresponds to the weight that a model reported assigning to that attribute when prompted explicitly. The weights the models reported meaningfully correlated with the weights that actually guided their decisions, and fine-tuning on examples of accurate reports further improved their accuracy. Right: The Pearson correlation between the models' reported and learned attribute weights before and after training (blue and purple, respectively). The reports of the base models that had not undergone this fine-tuning were almost entirely uncorrelated with the learned preferences (gray). Thus, the accuracy of the fine-tuned models must reflect their ability to report their new (fine-tuned) preferences and not an informed guess about their preferences based on their general background knowledge. Error bars indicate 95% HDIs.
annotation.annotation: The bar chart illustrates the self-report accuracy related to instilled preferences for two models, GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini, under different training conditions. The categories are displayed along the horizontal axis and include GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini, arranged in this order. The value axis is vertical, labeled as "Self-Report Accuracy (Instilled Preferences)" and ranges from 0.00 to 1.00 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 0.25. Each model category is represented by three bars: gray for "Control," light blue for "Before Introspection Training," and dark indigo for "After Introspection Training," as indicated in the legend. For GPT-4o, the gray bar is the shortest, at approximately 0.10, the light blue bar is around 0.55, and the dark indigo bar is nearly 0.75. For GPT-4o-mini, the gray bar is about -0.05, the light blue bar is approximately 0.50, and the dark indigo bar is around 0.75. Bars are grouped side by side within each model category, without any specific sorting, and no bars are visually emphasized.

annotation.annotation: The bar chart illustrates the accuracy percentages for different methods across three categories: Mathverse, MMLU, and Physics. The horizontal axis contains the categorical labels "Mathverse", "MMLU", and "Physics", with each category having grouped bars. The vertical axis represents accuracy, labeled "Accuracy (%)", with a linear scale ranging from 50% to 62% and tick labels at intervals of 2%. Each category features six bars that are color-coded and patterned according to a legend: DAPO+Self-reflection (solid blue), DAPO (blue with diagonal stripes), SRPO (solid orange), GRPO (orange with diagonal stripes), PPO+Self-reflection (solid green), and PPO (green with diagonal stripes). In Mathverse, the DAPO+Self-reflection bar reaches approximately 53%, while while the PPO bar is slightly above 53% and the DAPO + Self-reflection is slightly above 56% and remaining with 53-56%. For MMLU, bars range from slightly above 54% (PPO) to about 57% (SRPO), and in Physics, the DAPO+Self-reflection bar reaches close to 61%, with the PPO bar at approximately 57% and remaining are within these ranges. They do not follow any specific sorting order, and three bars have diagonal stripes in them. A legend is provided at top with the category and their bar.

annotation.annotation: The bar chart illustrates the accuracy percentages for different methods across three benchmarks: Mathverse, MMLU, and Physics. The horizontal axis contains the benchmarks which are, from left to right; Mathverse, MMLU, and Physics. Each category features six bars that are color-coded and patterned according to a legend: "DAPO+Self-reflection" (solid blue), DAPO (light blue with diagonal stripes), SRPO (solid orange), GRPO (light orange with diagonal stripes), "PPO+Self-reflection" (solid green), and PPO (light green with diagonal stripes). The PPO+Self-reflection bar is at roughly 54.5%, while the other bas trail behind at approximately 53.5%. Regarding MMLU, The DAPPO+Self-reflection and SRPO lead at roughly 57%, with the SPRO bar slightly higher. The PPO+Self-reflection follows slightly above 56%, and the DAPO and GRPO bars follow at slightly below 56%, with the PPO bar trailing at about 54.5%. In the Physics benchmark, the DAPO+Self-reflection bar reaches roughly 61%, with SPRO bar following at roughly 60.5%. The PPO+Self-reflection is at about 59%, followd by the GRPO bar with about 58%, the DAPO bar with roughly 57.5%, and the PPO bar coming in at about 57%. annotation.annotation: The bar chart illustrates the relationship between the number of shots and the corresponding values of _C in two categories: "Correct" and "Incorrect." The horizontal axis represents the "Number of Shots", labeled with integers ranging from 0 to 4. The vertical axis, labeled _C, uses a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 0.6, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The chart consists of grouped bars for each category of shots, where each group contains two bars with different patterns to distinguish between "Incorrect" and "Correct" outcomes. The "Incorrect" bars are blue with black dots pattern, and the values range approximately from 0.05 to 0.22. The "Correct" bars are shaded maroon with black diagonal lines and have values approximately between 0.3 and 0.6. For each group, the "Correct" bars are consistently taller than the "Incorrect" bars, except for shot number 4, where the difference is still there but not as big as others. The bars are arranged in numerical order according to the shot numbers without any apparent emphasis on specific bars. A legend is given on top-center.

annotation.annotation: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of samples of multi-genre Chinese writing for different text types across two categories: "Open" and "Cons." The vertical axis represents the sample count, labeled "Sample Count" with a linear scale from 0 to 140, marked at intervals of 20. Each text type category contains a pair of bars: the blue representing the "Open" category and the pink representing "Cons." In the "Argumentative" category, the blue bar for "Open" has a value of 79, while the pink bar for "Cons." is 122. The "Narrative" category shows the blue bar at 80 and the pink bar at 87. For "Descriptive" texts, the blue bar measures 68, and the pink bar is marked at 100. In the "Expository" category, the blue bar has a value of 62, and the pink bar is at 130. The bars are grouped by text type and do not appear to be sorted in a specific order. No bars are visually emphasized beyond their color coding for "Open" and "Cons." noted in the chart's legend. The bars for the "Cons." category are always higher than their "Open" counterparts.

annotation.annotation: The line plot illustrates the mean interclass similarity across different relation categories. The y-axis is labeled "Mean Interclass Similarity" and has a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 0.5 with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. The plot contains three primary lines. The first line is blue with circle markers and a solid style, representing "w/o DPO obo". It starts with a mean interclass similarity of slightly above 0.2 at 0 relational category, peaking around 0.5 at the 2nd and 31st category, and fluctuates across the axis, ending near 0.1. The second line is orange with triangle markers and a solid style, representing "w/o DPO obo & w/o div-hint". It starts just about 0.1, peaks multiple times with the highest point around 0.5 near the 40th category, and ends slightly below 0.1. The third line is green with square markers and a solid style, showing "DPO". This line begins near 0.17 and has fluctuations along the axis, ending just above the blue line and below the orange line. Additionally, there are three horizontal dashed lines representing average values: one orange at 0.158, one blue at 0.107, and one green at 0.086. All the line a multiple points intersect each other. A legend is given top left describing the line and its color.

annotation.caption: Average cosine similarity between generated training samples (K=32) for each relation category.
annotation.annotation: The plot illustrates the mean interclass similarity across different relation categories. The x-axis is labeled "Relation Category" and has a linear scale, ranging from approximately 0 to 60 with tick marks at intervals of 10. The y-axis is labeled "Mean Interclass Similarity" and has a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 0.5 with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. The plot contains three primary lines. The first line is blue with circle markers and a solid style, representing "w/o DPO obo." It starts at approximately 0.0, peaking around 0.5 at the 2nd category and 31st category, and fluctuates across the axis, ending near 0. The second line is orange with triangle markers and a solid style, representing "w/o DPO obo & w/o div-hint." It starts just above 0.1, peaks multiple times with the highest point around 0.45 near the 31st category, and ends slightly below 0.1. The third line is green with star markers and a solid style, showing "DPO." This line begins near 0.1 and maintains a relatively stable course, with minor fluctuations, ending just around 0.05. Additionally, there are three horizontal dashed lines representing average values: one orange at 0.158, one blue at 0.107, and one green at 0.086. A legend is provided at the top right of the plot to map different lines to their labels.

annotation.caption: Average repetition rate of words between generated training samples (K=32) for each relation category.
annotation.annotation: The line plot illustrates the mean interclass similarity across different relation categories. The x-axis is labeled "Relation Category" and has a linear scale, ranging from approximately 0 to 60 with tick marks at intervals of 10. The y-axis is labeled "Average Repetition Rate" and has a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 0.6 with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. The plot contains three primary lines. The first line is blue with circle markers and a solid style, representing "w/o DPO obo". It starts with a mean interclass similarity of slightly above 0.2 at 0 relational category, peaking around 0.6 at the 1st and 31st category, and fluctuates across the axis, ending below 0.1 at 64th category. The second line is orange with triangle markers and a solid style, representing "w/o DPO obo & w/o div-hint". It starts just about 0.16, peaks with the highest point around 0.6 near the 31st category, and ends about 0.16 at 64th category. The third line is green with square markers and a solid style, showing "DPO". This line begins near 0.117 and has fluctuations along the axis, peaks with the highest point around 0.6 near the 31st category, ending just above the blue line and below the orange line. Additionally, there are three horizontal dashed lines representing average values: one orange at 0.227, one blue at 0.163, and one green at 0.117. All the line a multiple points intersect each other. A legend is given top left describing the line and its color.

The blue line with circular markers and a solid style represents "w/o DPO obo," beginning at approximately 0.1, peaking around 0.5 near category 5, and ending around 0.1. The orange line with triangular markers and a solid style denotes "w/o DPO obo & w/o div-hint," also starting near 0.1, peaking at about 0.4 near category 6, and finishing around 0.2. The green line, featuring square markers and a solid style, signifies "DPO," starting around 0.1, fluctuating slightly, and ending near 0.1. Each line exhibits variability with several peaks and troughs throughout the range of categories. Horizontal dashed lines indicate average values: 0.227 for the orange line, 0.163 for the blue line, and 0.117 for the green line.

annotation.paper_title: Generating Diverse Training Samples for Relation Extraction with Large   Language Models
annotation.caption: Average repetition rate of words between generated training samples (K=32) for each relation category.
annotation.annotation: The plot illustrates the average repetition rate across different relation categories. The x-axis is labeled "Relation Category" and has a linear scale, ranging from approximately 0 to 60 with tick marks at 10-unit intervals. The y-axis is labeled "Average Repetition Rate" and has a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 0.6 with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. The plot contains three primary lines. The first line is blue with circle markers and a solid style, representing "w/o DPO obo." It starts at 0.26, peaking around 0.62 at the 31st category, and fluctuates across the axis, ending below 0.1. The second line is orange with triangle markers and a solid style, representing "w/o DPO obo & w/o div-hint." It starts just above 0.1, peaks multiple times with the highest point around 0.6 near the 31st category, and ends slightly below 0.2. The third line is green with stars markers and a solid style, showing "DPO." This line begins near 0.16 and maintains a relatively stable course, with minor fluctuations, ending just above 0.0. Additionally, there are three horizontal dashed lines representing average values: one orange at 0.227, one blue at 0.164, and one green at 0.117. A legend is provided at the top right of the plot to map different lines to their labels.
annotation.model_annotation: The plot illustrates the average repetition rate across different relation categories, comparing three scenarios. The x-axis represents the relation categories, labeled as "Relation Category," with a linear scale ranging from 0 to roughly 65, with tick labels at intervals of 5. The y-axis is labeled "Average Repetition Rate," also on a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 0.6 with tick labels at intervals of 0.1. The blue line with circular markers and a solid style represents "w/o DPO obo," beginning at approximately 0.1, peaking around 0.5 near category 5, and ending around 0.1. The orange line with triangular markers and a solid style denotes "w/o DPO obo & w/o div-hint," also starting near 0.1, peaking at about 0.4 near category 6, and finishing around 0.2. The green line, featuring square markers and a solid style, signifies "DPO," starting around 0.1, fluctuating slightly, and ending near 0.1. Each line exhibits variability with several peaks and troughs throughout the range of categories. Horizontal dashed lines indicate average values: 0.227 for the orange line, 0.163 for the blue line, and 0.117 for the green line.

annotation.paper_title: Generating Diverse Training Samples for Relation Extraction with Large   Language Models
annotation.caption: Average repetition rate of words between generated training samples (K=32) for each relation category.
annotation.annotation: The line plot illustrates the average repetition rate across different relation categories. The x-axis is labeled "Relation Category" and has a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 60 with tick marks at intervals of 10. The y-axis is labeled "Average Repetition Rate" and has a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 0.6 with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. The plot contains three primary lines. The first line is blue with circle markers and a solid style, representing "w/o DPO obo". It starts with a average repetition rate of slightly about 0.25 at 0 relational category, peaking at around 0.6 at the 1st and 31st category, and fluctuates across the axis, ending around 0.3 at 64th category. The second line is orange with triangle markers and a solid style, representing "w/o DPO obo & w/o div-hint". It starts just about 0.16, peaks with the highest point slightly under 0.6 near the 31st category, and ends about 0.16 at 64th category. The third line is green with square markers and a solid style, showing "DPO". This line begins near 0.163 and has fluctuations along the axis, peaks with the highest point around 0.6 near the 31st category, slightly below 0.1. Additionally, there are three horizontal dashed lines representing average values: one orange at 0.227, one blue at 0.163, and one green at 0.117. All the line a multiple points intersect each other. A legend is given top left describing the line and its color.
annotation.model_annotation: The plot illustrates the average repetition rate across different relation categories, comparing three scenarios. The x-axis represents the relation categories, labeled as "Relation Category," with a linear scale ranging from 0 to roughly 65, with tick labels at intervals of 5. The y-axis is labeled "Average Repetition Rate," also on a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 0.6 with tick labels at intervals of 0.1. The blue line with circular markers and a solid style represents "w/o DPO obo," beginning at approximately 0.1, peaking around 0.5 near category 5, and ending around 0.1. The orange line with triangular markers and a solid style denotes "w/o DPO obo & w/o div-hint," also starting near 0.1, peaking at about 0.4 near category 6, and finishing around 0.2. The green line, featuring square markers and a solid style, signifies "DPO," starting around 0.1, fluctuating slightly, and ending near 0.1. Each line exhibits variability with several peaks and troughs throughout the range of categories. Horizontal dashed lines indicate average values: 0.227 for the orange line, 0.163 for the blue line, and 0.117 for the green line.

annotation.paper_title: Generating Diverse Training Samples for Relation Extraction with Large   Language Models
annotation.caption: Average repetition rate of words between generated training samples (K=32) for each relation category.
annotation.annotation: The line plot illustrates the average repetition rate across different relation categories, comparing three scenarios. The x-axis represents the relation categories, labeled as "Relation Category," with a linear scale ranging from 0 to roughly 60, with tick labels at intervals of 10. The y-axis is labeled "Average Repetition Rate," also on a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 0.6 with tick labels at intervals of 0.1. The blue line with circular markers and a solid style represents "w/o DPO obo," beginning at approximately 0.25, peaking just above 0.6 near category 32, and ending around 0.1 and almost similar height near category 2. The orange line with triangular markers and a solid style denotes "w/o DPO obo & w/o div-hint," also starting just above 0.1, peaking at just below 0.6 near category 32, and finishing around 0.3. The green line, featuring square markers and a solid style, signifies "DPO," starting around 0.15, fluctuating slightly, with a peak at around 42nd category just above 0.2, and ending near 0.1. Each line exhibits variability with several peaks and troughs throughout the range of categories. Horizontal dashed lines indicate average values: 0.227 for the orange line, 0.163 for the blue line, and 0.117 for the green line. A legend is given top right describing the line and its color.

annotation.paper_title: Generating Diverse Training Samples for Relation Extraction with Large   Language Models
annotation.caption: Micro F1 (%) of KnowPrompt using different numbers of training samples generated by LLMs.
annotation.annotation: The line plot illustrates the performance of different datasets as measured by the Micro F1 score against the number of samples generated. The x-axis is labeled "Number of Samples Generated", with values of K=8, K=16, K=32, and K=64 marked at regular intervals, and it follows a linear scale without specified units. The y-axis is labeled "Micro F1 (%)" and also uses a linear scale, ranging from 25 to 50, with tick intervals of 5 percent. There are four lines in the plot: the blue line with circular markers represents TACRED, following a solid line style. It begins at approximately 22% at K=8 and slightly increases to around 30% by K=32, showing a minor downward trend after K=32. The orange line with triangular markers represents TACRED-Revisit, also solid; it starts just above the blue line at about 23% and ends at approximately 30%, showing a similar pattern as blue line with a peak at K=32. The green line with diamond markers represents Re-TACRED, increasing from around 35% at K=8 to about 51% at K=32 before slightly declining to around 47% at K=64. Lastly, the red line with star-shaped markers represents SemEval, steadily rising from about 42% at K=8 to approximately 53% at K=64, maintaining a consistent upward trend. Only the green and red line intercept each other. A legend is given on top left describing the line and the color.

There are four lines in the plot: the blue line with circular markers represents TACRED, following a solid line style. The green line with diamond markers represents Re-TACRED, increasing from around 35% at K=8 to about 44% at K=32 before slightly declining to around 41% at K=64. Lastly, the red line with star-shaped markers represents SemEval, steadily rising from about 42% at K=8 to approximately 48% at K=64, maintaining a consistent upward trend.

annotation.caption: Micro F1 (%) of KnowPrompt using different numbers of training samples generated by LLMs.
annotation.annotation: The plot illustrates the performance of different datasets as measured by the Micro F1 score against the number of samples generated. The x-axis is labeled "Number of Samples Generated," with categorical values of K=8, K=16, K=32, and K=64 marked. The y-axis is labeled "Micro F1 (%)" and also uses a linear scale, ranging from 20 to 50, with tick intervals of 5 percent. There are four lines in the plot: the blue line with circular markers represents TACRED, following a solid line style. It begins at approximately 22% at K=8 and slightly decreases to around 29% by K=64, showing a minor downward trend after K=32. The orange line with triangular markers represents TACRED-Revisit, also solid; it starts just above the blue line at about 23% and ends at approximately 30%, showing a similar pattern with a peak at K=32. The green line with diamond markers represents Re-TACRED, increasing from approximately 35% at K=8 to around 52% at K=32, before slightly declining to approximately 47% at K=64. Lastly, the red line with star-shaped markers represents SemEval, steadily rising from about 42% at K=8 to approximately 53% at K=64, maintaining a consistent upward trend. A legend is provided at the top left of the plot to map different lines to their labels.

annotation.annotation: The line plot illustrates the performance of different datasets as measured by the Micro F1 score against the number of samples generated. The y-axis is labeled "Micro F1 (%)" and also uses a linear scale, ranging from 20 to 50, with tick intervals of 5 percent. There are four lines in the plot: the blue line with circular markers represents TACRED, following a solid line style. It begins at approximately 23% at K=8 and slightly increases to around 28% by K=64, where its peak appears, and shows a minor downward trend after K=32. The orange line with triangular markers represents TACRED-Revisit, also solid; it also starts just above the blue line at approximately 23% , reaches a peak of 31% and ends at approximately 30%, showing a similar pattern with a peak at K=32. The green line with diamond markers represents Re-TACRED, increasing from around 35% at K=8 to about 51% at K=32 before slightly declining to around 47% at K=64. Lastly, the red line with star-shaped markers represents SemEval, steadily rising from about 42% at K=8 to approximately 53% at K=64, maintaining a consistent upward trend.A legend is provided at the top left of the plot to map different lines to their labels.

annotation.caption: The QA performance, confidence, and alignment of ChatGPT under different question popularity.
annotation.annotation: The plot illustrates how ChatGPT's Accuracy, Confidence, and Alignment change with Question Popularity on song-related questions. The x-axis is labeled "Question Popularity" and uses a linear scale ranging from 5 to 25 with tick labels at intervals of 5. The y-axis is labeled "Values" is also on a linear scale, ranging from 0.55 to 1.00 with tick labels at intervals of 0.05. The blue line, representing Accuracy, has circle markers and a solid line style. It starts around 0.65 at an x-value of 5, dips slightly to 0.60 at about a popularity of 6, and then generally increases, ending near 0.90 at an x-value of 25, with a noticeable rise after x=15. The green line, indicating Confidence, uses triangle markers and a solid line style, starting at about 0.93 at x=5 and maintaining a steady, slightly increasing trend with minor fluctuations, peaking at about 0.98 at x=25. The red line, representing Alignment, is depicted with square markers and a solid line style, starting at approximately 0.73 at x=5, experiencing fluctuations between 0.70 and 0.85, and finishing at around 0.90 at x=25, showing an upward trend toward the end.

annotation.annotation: The bar chart illustrates the correlation values between four different categories labeled as Pop_GT, Pop_GE, RPop_GT, and RPop_GE across three domains: Movies, Songs, and Basketball. The horizontal axis represents the categories Movies, Songs, and Basketball, while the vertical axis represents the correlation with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 0.7, marked at intervals of 0.1. Each domain has four grouped bars, each with a different color and pattern: Pop_GT in solid orange, Pop_GE in orange with crosshatch lines, RPop_GT in solid blue, and RPop_GE in blue with diagonal lines. In the Movies category, the bars indicate correlation values of approximately 0.2 for Pop_GT, 0.1 for Pop_GE, approximately 0.35 for RPop_GT, and around 0.6 for RPop_GE. In the Songs category, the values are about 0.3 for Pop_GT, around 0.1 for Pop_GE, 0.5 for RPop_GT, and 0.7 for RPop_GE. For Basketball, the values are approximately 0.06 for Pop_GT, 0.08 for Pop_GE, approximately 0.15 for RPop_GT, and 0.2 for RPop_GE. The bars are not sorted in any particular order, and there is no visible emphasis applied to any specific bar. A legend is provided on the top right of the plot to map different bar styles to their labels.

annotation.annotation: The bar chart illustrates the correlation values between four different categories labeled as "Pop_GT", "Pop_GE", "RPop_GT", and "RPop_GE" across three domains: Movies, Songs, and Basketball. The horizontal axis represents the categories "Movies", "Songs", and "Basketball", while the vertical axis represents the correlation with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 0.7, marked at intervals of 0.1. Each domain has four grouped bars, each with a different color and pattern: "Pop_GT" in solid orange, "Pop_GE" in orange with crosshatch lines, "RPop_GT" in solid blue, and "RPop_GE" in blue with crosshatch lines. In the Movies category, the bars indicate correlation values of approximately 0.2 for "Pop_GT", 0.1 for "Pop_GE", 0.35 for "RPop_GT", and 0.62 for "RPop_GE". In the Songs category, the values are about 0.3 for "Pop_GT", 0.1 for "Pop_GE", 0.5 for "RPop_GT", and 0.7 for "RPop_GE". For Basketball, the values are approximately 0.08 for "Pop_GT", 0.09 for "Pop_GE", 0.12 for "RPop_GT", and 0.2 for "RPop_GE". The bars are not sorted in any particular order, and there is no visible emphasis applied to any specific bar.

annotation.annotation: he bar chart illustrates the popularity of three categories: Movies, Songs, and Basketball based on different AI models represented with varying colors and patterns. The horizontal axis contains the categories labeled as Movies, Songs, and Basketball, while the vertical axis represents the popularity, with a linear scale ranging from 20 to 220 in increments of 20. Each category includes three stacked and patterned bars that represent different conditions: "Acc=0 & GT Ans," "Acc=0 & Gene Ans," and "Acc=1 & GT Ans." The AI models are color-coded with Llama3 in blue, Qwen2 in red, and ChatGPT in yellow. For Movies, each model's total bar height is approximately 20 to 60, with ChatGPT having the shortest total bar. In Songs, the heights range around 50 to 80, while in Basketball, all models show a marked increase with heights between approximately 100 to 200, with Qwen2 reaching the highest point at around 200. The bars are not sorted in any specific order beyond their categorical grouping, and there are no additional visual emphases such as bolding or shading on specific bars. A legend is provided on the top left of the bar chart to map different bar styles and colors to their labels.

annotation.annotation: The bar chart illustrates the popularity of three categories—Movies, Songs, and Basketball—based on different AI models represented with varying colors and patterns. The horizontal axis contains the categories labeled as Movies, Songs, and Basketball, while the vertical axis represents the popularity, with a linear scale ranging from 20 to 220 in increments of 20. Each category includes three stacked and patterned bars that represent different conditions: "Acc=0 & GT Ans" with mesh like pattern, "Acc=0 & Gene Ans" with diagnoal stripes, and "Acc=1 & GT Ans" with solid color. The AI models are color-coded with Llama3 in blue, Qwen2 in red, and ChatGPT in yellow. For Movies, each model's total bar height is approximately 25 to 50, with ChatGPT having the shortest total bar. In Songs, the heights range around 50 to 80, while in Basketball, all models show a marked increase with heights between approximately 95 to 200, with Qwen2 reaching the highest point at around 200. The bars are not sorted in any specific order beyond their categorical grouping, and there are no additional visual emphases such as bolding or shading on specific bars. A legend is given top left describing the bars and the patterns.

annotation.annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between answer popularity and three metrics: accuracy, confidence, and alignment, for ChatGPT on song-related data. The x-axis is labeled "Answer Popularity" with a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 160, with tick labels at intervals of 20. The y-axis is labeled "Values", also on a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. The blue line represents the "Accuracy" metric, characterized by circular markers and a solid line style. It reaches a low of approximately 0.5 at an answer popularity of 20 and ends at a high of 0.8 at 160, showing a rise with some fluctuations. The green line represents "Confidence," featuring triangular markers and a solid line style, starting around 0.9 at 20 and maintaining a generally steady high level, closing slightly higher around 0.95 at 160. The red line, representing "Alignment", uses square markers with a solid line style, beginning near 0.65 and increasing, finishing off around 0.8 towards the end of the x-axis. A legend is provided at the top of the chart to map different colors of lines to their labels.

annotation.annotation: The line plot illustrates the relationship between answer popularity and three parameters: accuracy, confidence, and alignment, for ChatGPT on basketball-related data. The y-axis is labeled "Values", also on a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The blue line represents accuracy, with circular markers and a solid style. It starts at approximately 0.3 at slightly above 0 popularity, decreases to about 0.2 at around 50, climbs steadily to around 0.55 at around 200, and slightly decreases towards 0.5 by 300. The green line denotes confidence, with triangular markers and a dashed style. It remains fairly steady around 0.8 throughout the entire range, starting slightly below 0.8 at slightly above 0 and ending around 0.79 at 300. The red line stands for alignment, with square markers and a dashed style. It begins near 0.55 at slightly above 0 popularity, dips to around 0.4 at 50, then rises steadily to about 0.7 at 200, maintaining a similar value towards the end at 300. The lines do not intersect. A legend is given bottom left describing the line and color.

annotation.paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
annotation.caption: We compare error rate (one minus accuracy), computation cost, and memory usage across our approach and baselines when fine-tuning Llama-3-8B on ten NLP tasks. MTL-FT refers to first fine-tuning a shared LoRA on all the datasets, and then fine-tuning the low-rank adapter on each dataset, while Full FT refers to full fine-tuning of the entire model. Our approach boosts the test accuracy of QLoRA by 10\% on average, only incurring 8\% additional computation and 9 GB more memory. It performs on par with the best baseline with 45\% less FLOPs.

annotation.paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
annotation.caption: We compare error rate (one minus accuracy), computation cost, and memory usage across our approach and baselines when fine-tuning Llama-3-8B on ten NLP tasks. MTL-FT refers to first fine-tuning a shared LoRA on all the datasets, and then fine-tuning the low-rank adapter on each dataset, while Full FT refers to full fine-tuning of the entire model. Our approach boosts the test accuracy of QLoRA by 10\% on average, only incurring 8\% additional computation and 9 GB more memory. It performs on par with the best baseline with 45\% less FLOPs.

annotation.paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
annotation.caption: Illustrating the empirical generalization errors and sharpness measures with respect to QLoRA weights. (<ref>) Smaller adapters with a rank of 16 achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima. (<ref>) An ensemble of k adapters leads to lower generalization errors and Hessian traces. Here, we fix the sum of the dimensions of k adapters to be equal to 256. (<ref>) QLoRA, which is trained on a quantized base model, yields lower generalization errors and Hessian trace values compared to LoRA.

annotation.caption: Illustrating the empirical generalization errors and sharpness measures with respect to QLoRA weights. (<ref>) Smaller adapters with a rank of 16 achieve the lowest generalization errors.
